messages:
Laura Bennett: Quick q for this group as we lock marketplace SKUs/pricing. We need a clear stance on (1) marketplace fee impact (AWS/GCP), (2) revrec treatment (gross vs net), and (3) how we represent credits/discounts in marketplace terms (private offers vs promo credits). Trying to unblock PMM copy + the pricing tables.

Rishi Malhotra: I pulled rough fee assumptions from our last model: AWS MP is effectively a % of billed (varies by program/contract), GCP MP similar. For modeling I’ve been using 10% as a planning placeholder unless we have a confirmed rate for our listing type.

Cole Summers: From the eng/billing side: our meters will still generate usage internally, but for MP buyers we’ll reconcile against the marketplace reports. Important: there’s no concept of “Redwood-issued free credits” on AWS MP invoices unless we do it as a discounted price plan/private offer.

Ben Carter: +1 — marketing wants to keep “$X free credits” in some onboarding messaging, but I’m worried that will be a compliance headache if the purchase is via marketplace.

Laura Bennett: Exactly. We can’t say “free credits” if the invoice goes through AWS/GCP and then we comp usage on our side. Procurement folks want a clean paper trail.

Jordan Blake: From field: buyers ask for (a) committed spend drawdown, (b) ability to apply enterprise discounts, (c) invoice line clarity. If we can’t do credits, we need a talk track: “use a private offer” or “use a lower rate SKU.”

Rishi Malhotra: Re: revrec — we need to decide principal vs agent. My assumption is we’re principal (we deliver the service; marketplace is a sales channel), so we recognize gross revenue and treat marketplace fee as a commission expense. But we should confirm with Legal + accounting policy.

Michael Grant: Jumping in. Principal/agent analysis: generally if Redwood controls the service delivery (SLA, provisioning, support) and sets pricing, we’re principal. AWS/GCP are payment processors/marketplaces. So revenue should be gross, fees recorded as selling expense (or contra-revenue depending on policy, but typically commission). Caveat: if marketplace terms impose material control over pricing/refunds, we should document but it’s usually still gross for SaaS.

Laura Bennett: Helpful. Can you send a short blurb we can paste into the internal doc? Something like “Recognize gross; fee is commission” with the caveat.

Michael Grant: Yep. I’ll draft a 3–4 sentence memo and drop in #finance later today.

Nikhil Sharma: On discounts: can we do “promo credits” as a Redwood internal entitlement add-on (like extra usage) without changing the marketplace price?

Laura Bennett: That’s the part I’m worried about. If we sell $100k via marketplace and then silently give $20k extra usage, procurement/accounting at the customer will ask why the contract/invoice doesn’t reflect it. Also partner reviewers sometimes flag off-invoice discounting.

Cole Summers: Also operationally messy: we’d be creating a parallel “credit ledger” that doesn’t reconcile to marketplace billed amount. Support tickets guaranteed.

Rishi Malhotra: Typical MP pattern is:
- Public offer = list price
- Private offer = negotiated net price (discount baked in)
- For “trial” you do a $0 or low-cost limited-term offer if allowed, or direct free trial off-marketplace before they buy.
We should avoid internal credits for MP buyers.

Ben Carter: So for marketing: we can still do “free credits” for direct sign-up, but for MP route we say “discounted private offer available” / “committed spend via marketplace private offer.”

Jordan Blake: Works for sales too. We can position it as: “If you need a discount, ask your AE for a private offer through AWS/GCP.”

Laura Bennett: Question: can private offers reflect one-time implementation fees / platform fees? Or are we constrained to usage-based line items?

Michael Grant: Depends on the marketplace product type and what’s permitted in the offer structure. Generally, you can structure as contract pricing for SaaS (e.g., annual fee) or usage pricing, but you can’t add arbitrary side letters in the marketplace paperwork. Any non-standard terms should be handled via direct contract, not the marketplace order form.

Rishi Malhotra: Fee impact modeling: if we’re doing private offer at discounted rates, the marketplace fee applies to the discounted billings (not list). So effective margin hit is fee % regardless of discount, but our gross margin drops because net revenue drops too.

Laura Bennett: Yep. That’s why we need a clear “floor” for marketplace pricing. We can’t stack: discount + fee + heavy COGS workloads.

Cole Summers: From metering/invoicing angle: for marketplace, invoice description is basically the SKU description + usage quantity. We should keep SKU names tight and avoid “includes $X credits” language in the SKU itself.

Nikhil Sharma: How do we represent “first 30 days free” then? Some competitors do it.

Rishi Malhotra: If we need it, it should be a separate marketplace offer/SKU with $0 price for a limited period or limited units (if allowed). Otherwise: “Free trial available via Redwood direct signup” and then convert to MP for procurement.

Ben Carter: That’s consistent with our funnel anyway. We can guide enterprise: test via direct, then shift spend to MP once procurement kicks in.

Jordan Blake: Note: some customers can’t run direct at all (policy). For those, we should have a default private offer template that’s effectively a “trial” (small committed amount) rather than $0.

Laura Bennett: Action items:
1) Rishi: update the pricing model doc w/ fee placeholder + sensitivity (e.g., 5/10/15%).
2) Michael: send revrec memo (gross vs net) + any language constraints.
3) Ben: update PMM guidance: no “free credits” language for MP; push “private offer discount” wording.
4) Cole: confirm any constraints on negative line items / crediting in our billing integration.

Cole Summers: On (4): we can’t do negative usage to represent credits. We can add internal entitlements, but it won’t show on marketplace invoice. So recommendation: only discount via private offer (price plan) so invoice matches what customer expects.

Laura Bennett: Great. I’ll summarize in the packaging thread so PMs stop asking for “marketplace credits.” :thumbsup:

Rishi Malhotra: I’ll also add a note: marketplace fees should be treated as a channel cost; for margin reporting, we should show both gross margin (COGS only) and contribution margin (COGS + MP fees) for MP-sourced spend.

Laura Bennett: +1. That’ll make exec reviews less confusing.

Michael Grant: Dropping quick draft memo later today. Also: careful with language like “invoice through AWS/GCP” — we should say “billed via marketplace” and avoid implying AWS/GCP provides the service.

Ben Carter: Noted. I’ll align listing copy accordingly.

Laura Bennett: Thanks all. Closing the loop once Michael’s memo is in.
